description: Whole-layer persistent monokernel with in-kernel peer exchanges (sgl-amd-mono: Muse Spark target / draft layer, GLM flash, Kimi ...): ONE launch a layer runs attention over the paged KV cache, o_proj + TP all-reduce, router / top-k, the experts + EP exchange and the next layer's QKV / KV write, pairing with its peer ranks through IPC peer buffers and epoch-tagged mailboxes. Correctness runs through call() and the rank harness; timing is rank_chain (shared/rank_timing.py): every rank times CUDA-graph replays of a chain of distinct layers.

rows.doc: tokens of the step (verify rows: requests x draft tokens)

context.doc: a request's keys including the step's rows (the census context); size the KV pool and page table from it

world.doc: TP/EP ranks of the deployment; timing runs exactly this many

stream.doc: the residual stream entering the layer (replicated over the TP ranks); the launch updates it in place, so call() clones

attn_input.doc: the layer's attention input (replicated over the TP ranks)

stream_out.doc: every rank's residual stream after the step -- compare all ranks, not rank 0

call: A rank harness (references/collective-ut.md) runs the deployed runner's launches on every rank for one step and returns all ranks' outputs stacked; host setup (page tables, cache save/restore, input distribution) is part of call() and therefore must never be what is timed. Timing goes through rank_chain(), not call().

timing.doc: shared/rank_timing.py. cases.rank_chain(rank, world, group, case) builds, OUTSIDE the timed window, a chain of chain_length DISTINCT layers (own weights and KV caches, so weights are L2/MALL-cold as in a ~60-layer step) at the case's rows and context, and exposes step(n) = bootstrap + n chained launches + epoch bump (graph-safe), check() = guard error words, close(). Per-launch ms = (T[step(length)] - T[step(short)]) / (length - short) of CUDA-graph replays, all ranks after a barrier, the bucket = max over ranks. Method of the Muse Spark layer team's frozen bench (bench_worker.target_chain) and sgl-amd-mono test/kernels.

negative_controls: drop a stage's contribution (the attention's softmax scale, the o_proj all-reduce's peer partials, an expert's routing score): the residual stream moves by ~|stream| on every rank
skip one peer's partial in the in-kernel all-reduce: rank outputs diverge from each other and from the baseline
pitfalls: Timing call() measures the host: a rank harness driving its peers over gloo, building page tables on the CPU and gathering outputs is ~100 ms against a ~0.15 ms launch (Muse Spark target layer, 2026-11-09). Time rank_chain only.

Eager timing is launch-bound: every FlyDSL launch costs ~135-170 us from the host regardless of work (sgl-amd-mono test_muse_spark_layer, MI355X), so a host-side Python change posts a fake speedup the served CUDA graph never sees.
One warm layer replayed over and over keeps its ~0.8 GB of weights in MALL; serving reads ~60 distinct layers a step. Chain distinct layers.
Contexts must be the served ones: a full-attention layer at 59k-566k keys costs far more than at 1k-8k; size the KV pool from the case.

Peer buffers and mailbox tags are collective state: every rank runs the same graphs, the same replay counts, in the same order, and the epoch advances once a step. A rank that stops early leaves the others spinning until the guard deadline -- a deadline hit is a FAILED measurement, never a slow one.
Exactly one device launch per layer call is part of the kernel's contract (MUSE_MONO_PROFILE launch audit); a candidate that splits the launch must be rejected even if faster in isolation.
Routing ids must stay bit-exact against the baseline (deterministic FP32 router); the float outputs within the baseline's own repeat noise.
